canvas-01.description: The lower half of sheet 1, drawn at 50 ft to an inch below the key map and index, shows the Minotola Plant of the Illinois Glass Co., marked as not in operation, on the triangle of ground between the two railroads at the north-east edge of Minotola. Central Avenue runs along the left edge. The double track of the C.R.R. of N.J. and Landisville Road run diagonally up to the north-east across the upper part, with a small Minotola Station of that line beside the tracks; the P.R.R. (West Jersey and Seashore Division) crosses the lower part with its own Minotola Station on Railroad Avenue, which runs along the bottom. Laura Place, marked arbitrary, runs down the right edge from S.E. Boulevard, with a single dwelling beyond it. The plant is drawn in detail: two furnace buildings (Plant 1 and Plant 2) with their lehrs and packing houses, a batch house of iron with wood purlins and trestle, a gas producer house, a coal house and 50,000 gallon cistern, a machine and pattern shop, a woodworking shop with blacksmith, offices and a sample room near Central Avenue, a long stock house, a paint house, a brick shed, fuel oil tanks, a well house, a hose cart house and paper storage. Long warehouses for crates, finished products and shipping stand along the P.R.R. siding and towards Laura Place. A 4 inch water pipe network with hydrants and hose is drawn through the yard, and a note describes the night watchmen, clock, private water system from artesian wells, the 50,000 gallon cistern and a Barr duplex steam fire pump. The rest of the ground, block 17, is vacant. Sheet 2 adjoins across Railroad Avenue and sheet 4 beyond Laura Place.
notes: Drawn at 50 ft to an inch, twice the scale of the other sheets.
Placed from two block corners carried from sheets 2 and 4 (Central Avenue at Railroad Avenue, and Laura Place at S.E. Boulevard); no modern street junction is drawn on the part.

The fitted scale between the two carried corners is about 7 percent smaller than the drawn 50 ft scale bar, so the drawing between Central Avenue and Laura Place is either compressed or one of the carried corners is a few metres off.
The P.R.R. (West Jersey and Seashore) line through the plant has been abandoned; the C.R.R. of N.J. line is now the Southern Running Track.
Laura Place is marked arbitrary; Liberty Drive runs near it today but not on its line.
The Illinois Glass Co. Minotola Plant is marked not in operation.

Sheet 1. Top half: key map at 800 ft to an inch (Minotola and Landisville), legend, title cartouche, water facilities and fire department notes, street and specials index: not georeferenced. Bottom half below a heavy line: Illinois Glass Co. Minotola Plant (not in operation) at 50 ft to an inch, between the C.R.R. of N.J. and Landisville Road on the north and the P.R.R. (West Jersey and Seashore Division) and Railroad Avenue on the south, Central Avenue at the left edge, Laura Place (arbitrary) and S.E. Boulevard at the right edge. One part (the plant). Result: config canvas-01 placed from two block corners carried from sheet-2-1 (Central Av / Railroad Av) and sheet-4 (Laura Pl / S.E. Blvd); helmert, low confidence. The two corners are 7 percent closer on the sheet than on the ground at the drawn 50 ft scale; config scale_ft 53.5 keeps the second pass from forcing 50 ft (which put each corner 11 m off and Central Av 11 m west of its drawn line).

sheet-2-1.description: The main part of sheet 2, drawn at 100 ft to an inch, covers the residential core of Minotola from Railroad Avenue and the P.R.R. (West Jersey and Seashore Division) at the top down to William Avenue, and from the blocks west of West Avenue to Cass Avenue on the right. Central Avenue, 80 ft wide with a 4 inch water pipe, runs down the middle; the cross streets are Atlantic, Summer, Pacific, Artic, Jonas and William Avenues, with 20 ft alleys through the middle of most blocks. The commercial buildings stand on Central Avenue near Atlantic Avenue: a bank, several stores of concrete block, an automobile repair shop, a feed store and a building marked to be the fire department. The Minotola Apron Co. factory stands at the top left on block 29, beside a vacant clothing manufacturing building, and a bottling works, a feed mill and a feed warehouse lie along Jonas Avenue near Central. Institutions are the Minotola Public School on Pacific Avenue west of Central, the First M.E. Church on Central between Summer and Pacific, and a Roman Catholic church with a vacant lot west of West Avenue near Jonas. The rest is frame dwellings, mostly pairs of two-storey double houses built to a pattern, on long narrow lots, with large empty lots in blocks 38, 41, 42, 44 and 45. William Avenue east of West Avenue is marked not opened. The upper left corner of the sheet holds a separate inset (part 2); Minotola station and the glass works are on sheet 1 across Railroad Avenue.
notes: Artic Avenue is spelled so on the sheet; it is East and West Arctic Avenue today.
William Avenue is Williams Avenue today; east of West Avenue it is marked not opened.
Central Avenue is South Central Avenue and West Avenue is South West Avenue today.
Railroad Avenue along the P.R.R. has no modern counterpart in the reference data; the railroad itself is abandoned.
The Minotola Public School, the First M.E. Church and a Roman Catholic church are on this part; the Minotola Apron Co. factory is at the top.

Minotola, 100 ft. Main part: Central Av, West Av, Cass Av with Railroad Av, Atlantic, Summer, Pacific, Artic, Jonas and William Avs; Minotola Public School, M.E. and R.C. churches, Minotola Apron Co. Part 2: inset at upper left behind a heavy line, the blocks east of Cass Av between Summer Av and Pacific Av (blocks 48, 49), continuing the main part to the east. Result: part 1 14 automatic GCPs, RMSE 1.1 m, LOO 1.5 m. Part 2 (inset) helmert from Cass/Summer and Cass/Pacific only, low confidence; its mask starts at the west edge of Cass Av and the south edge of Summer Av so its blank margin does not hide the main part.

sheet-2-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 2 is an inset in the upper left corner, behind a heavy line, drawn at 100 ft to an inch with its own north arrow. It continues the main part of the sheet eastwards across Cass Avenue: it shows Cass Avenue along its left edge and the blocks east of it between Summer Avenue at the top and the ground south of Pacific Avenue, blocks 48 and 49, cut through by a 20 ft alley. The lots are long and narrow, and the only buildings are three pairs of two-storey frame double dwellings on each side of the alley and on Pacific Avenue, built to the same pattern as those on the main part, and a single dwelling and a chicken coop on block 49. The margin beyond the lots is marked no exposure. A sheet number 2 at the top left and at the left edge refers back to this sheet, and a fragment of a block 2 outline is drawn above Summer Avenue.
notes: Inset east of Cass Avenue; it adjoins the right edge of the main part of the same sheet.

Placed from only two junctions on Cass Avenue (Summer Avenue and Pacific Avenue), as a similarity transformation; position across Cass Avenue and the east end of the lots are not independently checked.

Minotola, 100 ft. Main part: Central Av, West Av, Cass Av with Railroad Av, Atlantic, Summer, Pacific, Artic, Jonas and William Avs; Minotola Public School, M.E. and R.C. churches, Minotola Apron Co. Part 2: inset at upper left behind a heavy line, the blocks east of Cass Av between Summer Av and Pacific Av (blocks 48, 49), continuing the main part to the east. Result: part 1 14 automatic GCPs, RMSE 1.1 m, LOO 1.5 m. Part 2 (inset) helmert from Cass/Summer and Cass/Pacific only, low confidence; its mask starts at the west edge of Cass Av and the south edge of Summer Av so its blank margin does not hide the main part.

sheet-3-1.description: The main part of sheet 3, drawn at 100 ft to an inch, covers the north-west of Landisville between Grove Road and S.W. Boulevard with the C.R.R. of N.J. along the bottom edge. Grove Road crosses the upper half diagonally; Willow and Laurel Streets run from it down to S.W. Boulevard, Franklin and Nixon Streets run south from Arbor Avenue, and Tuckahoe Road comes in at an angle from the north-east, crossing Hudson Avenue near the right edge. Buena Vista Avenue, marked not opened, is shown as a dashed line on the right. Most of the ground is laid out in long narrow lots with scattered frame dwellings, sheds and chicken coops, and several blocks are still empty. The large block 17 west of Willow Street and the ground north of Grove Road are open land with only a few dwellings and outbuildings plotted without lot lines. The institutions are the Buena Vista Township Public School, a brick building on Grove Road between Laurel and Franklin Streets, and a Roman Catholic church on Nixon Street near S.W. Boulevard; a vacant factory stands on Franklin Street, and an automobile repair shop on Tuckahoe Road at the boulevard. Block 26 between Nixon Street and Tuckahoe Road narrows to the south because Tuckahoe Road runs at an angle to the grid. The area east of Tuckahoe Road between Arbor Avenue and S.W. Boulevard is drawn separately as an inset in the upper right corner (part 2), and sheets 4 and 5 adjoin across the railroad.
notes: Grove Road is Forest Grove Road today, Tuckahoe Road is Harding Highway (US 40), and Hudson Avenue appears to be Melini Avenue; the Melini Avenue junction was left out because its residual was over 6 m.
S.W. Boulevard (north of the railroad) is West North Boulevard today.
Buena Vista Avenue north of the railroad is marked not opened and has no modern counterpart on its line.
The Buena Vista Township Public School and a Roman Catholic church are on this part.

Landisville, 100 ft. Main part: Grove Road to S.W. Boulevard, Willow, Laurel, Franklin, Nixon and Tuckahoe Road, Arbor Av, Hudson Av and Buena Vista Av (not opened); Buena Vista Township Public School, R.C. church. Part 2: inset at upper right behind a heavy line, the blocks east of Tuckahoe Road between Arbor Av and S.W. Boulevard (Tuckahoe, Auburn, blocks 27, 28; Landisville Public School, Model Blouse Co., Joseph Lolli, Fruit Growers Assn). Result: part 1 13 automatic GCPs, RMSE 2.5 m, LOO 3.3 m (Harding Hwy / Melini Av excluded, 6.4 m). Part 2 4 automatic GCPs at the inset corners, RMSE 1.4 m, medium-low confidence.

sheet-3-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 3 is an inset in the upper right corner behind a heavy line, drawn at 100 ft to an inch. It shows the blocks of Landisville east of Tuckahoe Road between Arbor Avenue at the top and S.W. Boulevard and the C.R.R. of N.J. at the bottom, with Auburn Street crossing the middle; Buena Vista Avenue is marked leaving Arbor Avenue to the north. Block 27, between Tuckahoe Road and Auburn Street, holds the Landisville Public School on Arbor Avenue, the woodworking shop of D. Bigi with a gasoline engine, the Model Blouse Co. factory near S.W. Boulevard, and a row of stores and dwellings, some of concrete block, facing Tuckahoe Road. Block 28, east of Auburn Street, has the buildings of Joseph Lolli at Arbor Avenue and the Fruit Growers Association near the boulevard, with a few dwellings between. Notes on the Model Blouse Co. and Lolli premises record no watchman or fire apparatus, gasoline engine power and electric light still to come. The inset joins the main part of the sheet along Tuckahoe Road; sheet 5 adjoins across the railroad.
notes: Tuckahoe Road is Harding Highway (US 40) today and S.W. Boulevard east of it is North East Boulevard.

Placed from four junctions at the corners of the inset (Tuckahoe Road and Auburn Street at Arbor Avenue and at S.W. Boulevard); the Tuckahoe Road / Arbor Avenue junction lies just outside the inset's edge.
The Landisville Public School, the Model Blouse Co., D. Bigi woodworking, Joseph Lolli and the Fruit Growers Association are on this part.

Landisville, 100 ft. Main part: Grove Road to S.W. Boulevard, Willow, Laurel, Franklin, Nixon and Tuckahoe Road, Arbor Av, Hudson Av and Buena Vista Av (not opened); Buena Vista Township Public School, R.C. church. Part 2: inset at upper right behind a heavy line, the blocks east of Tuckahoe Road between Arbor Av and S.W. Boulevard (Tuckahoe, Auburn, blocks 27, 28; Landisville Public School, Model Blouse Co., Joseph Lolli, Fruit Growers Assn). Result: part 1 13 automatic GCPs, RMSE 2.5 m, LOO 3.3 m (Harding Hwy / Melini Av excluded, 6.4 m). Part 2 4 automatic GCPs at the inset corners, RMSE 1.4 m, medium-low confidence.

sheet-4.description: Sheet 4, drawn at 100 ft to an inch, covers the centre of Landisville south of the C.R.R. of N.J., from S.W. and S.E. Boulevards at the top down to Downs Avenue, and from the open block 47 on the left to Buena Vista Avenue on the right. The north-south streets are Willow, Laurel, Franklin and Nixon Streets and Buena Vista Avenue, all 66 ft wide; Flower, Delaware and Downs Avenues cross them. S.W. Boulevard is drawn north of the tracks with only the outlines of the blocks on sheet 3 beyond it. Between the tracks and S.E. Boulevard stand the Landisville Station with its freight house and passenger room. The business frontage is along S.E. Boulevard: stores and dwellings with stores, a feed warehouse, a hardware store, an automobile repair shop, a lumber yard on block 50 and the fire department, a small frame and concrete block building on block 53. A long chicken coop crosses block 52, and the rest of the blocks hold frame dwellings, coops and sheds on large lots, thinning out to almost empty blocks 63, 69, 70 and 71 towards Downs Avenue. At the left edge Laura Place and a short street lettered Hunter (arbitrary) lead west to sheet 1 past block 46, and a railroad siding curves off the main line to sheet 1. In the lower left corner the P.R.R. (West Jersey and Seashore Division) crosses diagonally beside Summer Avenue, an 80 ft road, past blocks 48 and 49 and block 68.
notes: S.W. Boulevard (north of the railroad) is West North Boulevard today and S.E. Boulevard (south of it) is West South Boulevard.
Downs Avenue is West Summer Road today; Flower Avenue is West Flower Street and Delaware Avenue is West Delaware Avenue.
Hunter, marked arbitrary, lies on the line of the modern Fiocchi Street; Laura Place, also arbitrary, was not matched to a modern street.
The P.R.R. (West Jersey and Seashore) line in the lower left is abandoned; the C.R.R. of N.J. is now the Southern Running Track.
The Landisville Station, the fire department and a lumber yard are on this sheet.

Landisville, 100 ft. S.W. and S.E. Boulevards and the C.R.R. of N.J. at the top, Willow, Laurel, Franklin, Nixon, Buena Vista Av; Flower, Delaware and Downs Avs; Hunter (arbitrary) and Laura Pl at the left; P.R.R. and Summer Av at lower left; Landisville station and freight house. One part. Result: 20 automatic GCPs, second order, RMSE 0.85 m, LOO 1.2 m. Pilot sheet; detector ink_below_paper 60 (138 found 15).

sheet-5-1.description: The main part of sheet 5, drawn at 100 ft to an inch, covers eastern Landisville. Its upper band runs from Buena Vista Avenue on the left to Summer Street on the right between S.E. Boulevard and Flower Avenue, crossed by Tuckahoe Road, Auburn, Bache, Forsythe and Clara Streets; above it are the C.R.R. of N.J. with a section house, S.W. Boulevard and the edges of blocks 27 and 28 of sheet 3 with a fertilizer warehouse and a basket warehouse. Below Flower Avenue the part continues on the left only, with Buena Vista Avenue, Tuckahoe Road, Delaware Avenue and Downs Avenue. Tuckahoe Road runs at an angle to the grid, so blocks 54, 55, 65 and 73 beside it are wedge-shaped. The business buildings line Tuckahoe Road: stores and dwellings with stores, a bakery, a wholesale furniture store, a flour store, two automobile repair shops, a lodge hall, a feed store and a garage with gasoline tanks. The Landisville Elec. Light Co. on block 56 at S.E. Boulevard shares a concrete building with a basket factory and a basket warehouse, with a 50,000 gallon water tank; a livery stands on Auburn Street. Blocks 57, 58, 59 and 72 east and south of the business street are large and nearly empty, with a few dwellings and coops. Railroad Avenue is marked leaving S.E. Boulevard at the upper right corner. The lower right of the sheet, behind a heavy line, is a separate part (part 2).
notes: S.E. Boulevard is South Boulevard and, east of Forsythe Street, South East Boulevard in the modern data; it is drawn 100 ft wide, and the run uses that width.
Summer Street is Sumner Street today, Bache Street is Bache Drive, and Tuckahoe Road is South Harding Highway (US 40); Downs Avenue is West and East Summer Road.
The Landisville Elec. Light Co. with a basket factory, a bakery, a lodge hall and a livery are on this part.

Landisville east, 100 ft. Main part (L-shaped): S.W./S.E. Boulevards to Flower Av from Buena Vista Av to Summer St (Tuckahoe Road, Auburn, Bache, Forsythe, Clara), and below Flower Av at the left Buena Vista Av, Tuckahoe Road, Delaware and Downs Avs; Landisville Elec. Light Co. Part 2: lower right behind a heavy line, turned so that the railroad runs diagonally: Francis H. Leggett Inc. pure food products plant on the C.R.R. of N.J. between S.W. Boulevard (not opened), S.E. Boulevard and Railroad Av, with Summer and Plymouth Streets. Result: part 1 17 automatic GCPs, RMSE 1.9 m, LOO 2.5 m; S.E. Boulevard drawn 100 ft (street_widths). Part 2: 2 automatic (Railroad Av at Summer and Plymouth) + 2 hand-picked on S.E. Blvd; the second pass dropped the hand-picked Summer St point (9 m); config scale_ft 101.6 holds the part's own fitted scale, low-medium confidence.

sheet-5-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 5 is the lower right quarter of the sheet, behind a heavy line, drawn at 100 ft to an inch and in the same orientation as the main part, but showing ground further east: Summer Street runs down its left edge and Plymouth Street down its right edge. The C.R.R. of N.J. crosses diagonally, curving to the north-east, between S.W. Boulevard on its north side, marked not opened, and S.E. Boulevard on its south side; Railroad Avenue, 100 ft wide, runs straight along the bottom. The upper part of the area is the plant of Francis H. Leggett Inc., manufacturers of pure food products, on block 28 beside the railroad: a warehouse and packing house, a factory with a platform and storage under it, an office, lockers, a garage, a pipe shop and storage, a long crate warehouse, and an engine and boiler room with a 10,000 gallon water tank, connected to the track by a trestle. A note records two watchmen, electric light and power and steam heat. Block 76 between S.E. Boulevard and Railroad Avenue holds a few dwellings, coops and a water tank, and a row of small buildings stands south of Railroad Avenue at Summer Street. A dwelling stands east of Plymouth Street. The margin along the right edge is marked no exposure.
notes: Railroad Avenue is South East Boulevard in the modern data, and S.E. Boulevard along the railroad is South Boulevard; Summer Street is Sumner Street.
S.W. Boulevard north of the railroad is marked not opened.

Placed from two detected junctions on Railroad Avenue and two hand-picked points on S.E. Boulevard at Summer and Plymouth Streets; the drawn distance between Summer and Plymouth Streets is about 2 percent shorter than the modern one.
The Francis H. Leggett Inc. pure food products plant is on this part.

Landisville east, 100 ft. Main part (L-shaped): S.W./S.E. Boulevards to Flower Av from Buena Vista Av to Summer St (Tuckahoe Road, Auburn, Bache, Forsythe, Clara), and below Flower Av at the left Buena Vista Av, Tuckahoe Road, Delaware and Downs Avs; Landisville Elec. Light Co. Part 2: lower right behind a heavy line, turned so that the railroad runs diagonally: Francis H. Leggett Inc. pure food products plant on the C.R.R. of N.J. between S.W. Boulevard (not opened), S.E. Boulevard and Railroad Av, with Summer and Plymouth Streets. Result: part 1 17 automatic GCPs, RMSE 1.9 m, LOO 2.5 m; S.E. Boulevard drawn 100 ft (street_widths). Part 2: 2 automatic (Railroad Av at Summer and Plymouth) + 2 hand-picked on S.E. Blvd; the second pass dropped the hand-picked Summer St point (9 m); config scale_ft 101.6 holds the part's own fitted scale, low-medium confidence.
